claims: Ps2FpuCvtWS checks the binary32 biased-exponent field before casting, saturates signs when the field exceeds 0x9d, and therefore avoids an out-of-range signed float-to-integer conversion for its in-range branch.
Ps2FpuMinS and Ps2FpuMaxS produce Sony's signed-zero result table for all four zero-sign pairs, and the emitted snippets clear only the O/U cause bits.
Ps2FpuSqrtS preserves signed zeros, maps negative normal finite inputs through sqrtf(abs(x)), sets I and sticky I, clears I/D cause bits, and leaves unrelated FCR31 bits unchanged.
The experimental sqrt helper is not a proof of bit-exact EE rounding for arbitrary non-perfect-square inputs.

evidence.text: Ps2FpuCvtWS extracts `bits & 0x7f800000u`; if greater than `0x4e800000u`, it returns sign-dependent INT32_MAX/MIN; otherwise it casts value to int32_t. Ps2FpuMinS returns -0 if either input is negative zero when both compare equal to zero; otherwise fs<=ft ? fs : ft. Ps2FpuMaxS returns -0 only if both zero operands have negative sign; otherwise fs>=ft ? fs : ft. The emitted MIN/MAX format strings clear `ctx->fcr31 &= ~0x0000c000u`. Ps2FpuSqrtS returns original sqrtf host path for exponent-255 and denormal operands; for supported finite inputs it clears only mask 0x00030000, preserves zero unchanged, handles negative inputs by sqrtf(abs(value)), ORs 0x00020000 and 0x40, and otherwise uses sqrtf(value).

Sony EE Core Instruction Set Manual v6.0: printed p.356 says CVT.W.S rounds toward zero and clamps if the biased exponent exceeds 0x9d: positive to 0x7fffffff, negative to 0x80000000. Printed p.365 gives MIN.S selection and clears O/U flags. Printed p.376 says SQRT.S returns sqrt(abs(x)) for negative inputs, sets I/SI, preserves signed zero, and D cause is cleared.

The experimental package README says the probe checks exact roots (including sqrt(-4)); it does not prove EE-specific square-root rounding for arbitrary values. The helper uses host sqrtf and makes no hardware equivalence claim.

disposition: Four claims verified, zero contradicted or unsupported, zero escalated for human review. Review assessed support and stated limitations, not hardware fidelity.
